meta.purpose: Real, sourced figures so vehicle customization in SLATE has real downstream effects (condition/value, theft, tint enforcement, tires, modification disclosure, dashcams/cameras, remote start/audio).
meta.fieldConventions: Each figure: value, unit, currency, url, publisher, date, sourceType, confirmed. confirmed=true only where the figure was read on the cited page/document in this session (WebFetch, curl or PDF text extraction). confirmed=false means seen only in a search-engine summary or a secondary site. Derived values are marked sourceType 'derived' and list their inputs.

kbbGrades.note: KBB's consumer tool uses four grades (a fifth, Poor, is not offered for valuation). KBB says it posts the share of vehicles matching each grade but only the Excellent share was readable in the FAQ.

shareExcellent.quote: if only 3% of the vehicles in the market are considered "Excellent" condition, chances are that your car isn't one of them

mostCommonGrade.quote: Most cars we see are in 'Good' Condition.

kbbGrades.valueDifferenceNote: KBB, Edmunds and Black Book do not publish a fixed percent or dollar gap between grades; the gap is computed per vehicle in their tools. Nothing citable.

gradeDefinitions.Excellent: Looks new, excellent mechanical condition, needs no reconditioning, never had paint or body work, free of rust.
gradeDefinitions.Very Good: Minor cosmetic defects, excellent mechanical condition, minor paint touch-ups and/or bodywork, minimal reconditioning.
gradeDefinitions.Good: Free of major defects, clean title; paint, body and interior have only minor (if any) blemishes.
gradeDefinitions.Fair: Some mechanical or cosmetic defects, needs servicing, still in reasonable running condition.
gradeDefinitions.publisher: Kelley Blue Book (as summarised by search engine)
gradeDefinitions.howModsMoveGrades: By these definitions: any repaint/bodywork (e.g., fixing curb rash or paint damage by refinishing) disqualifies Excellent; minor touch-ups = Very Good ceiling; visible blemishes/interior wear = Good; unrepaired cosmetic defects = Fair.

shareOutstanding.note: Page returned 403; figure from search summary.

edmundsGrades.definitionsSummary: Outstanding: no visible wear, glossy paint, near-new tires. Clean: minimal wear, glossy paint with slight scratches or dings, minimal interior fading, substantial tread. Average: some mechanical/cosmetic problems, typical wear. Rough: multiple mechanical or cosmetic problems. Damaged: major damage, not appraised.

blackBookGrades.note: Black Book grade names widely reported; no public percent gap.

ukUndisclosedModsLaw.value: Consumer Insurance (Disclosure and Misrepresentation) Act 2012: careless misrepresentation -> insurer may avoid only if it would not have offered cover at all, must refund premium; if it would have offered on different terms, claim is adjusted proportionately; deliberate/reckless -> avoid and keep premium
ukUndisclosedModsLaw.unit: legal rule as applied by FOS
ukUndisclosedModsLaw.publisher: Financial Ombudsman Service (decision DRN-4959020, Highway Insurance)
ukUndisclosedModsLaw.caseOutcome: Aftermarket alloys fitted two days before cover; policy excluded all mods; misrepresentation found careless not reckless: insurer entitled to avoid policy and refuse the multi-car collision claim and recover its costs, but must refund premium (offset against its outlay).

fosGuidance.value: Mods to declare include body kits, custom paint, alloy wheels (esp. oversized), ECU remaps, exhaust upgrades, tinted windows, stereo upgrades; undisclosed mods can void the policy, cause claims to be rejected, or raise premiums; a simple air-filter change was held not a reportable modification
